## Body

#303/#305 (fleet-map standalone):
- Script-block breakout proof is simple and complete: count `<` in the inlined text. HTML script-data state can only leave on `<`, so zero `<` (JSON with `<` -> \u003c, header constant `<`-free) closes </script, <!--, <script. U+2028/2029 and `-->` are irrelevant. Check the splice uses split/template, not String.replace (`$&` expansion).
- esc() in a style="" attribute stops attribute breakout but NOT CSS injection (url(https://evil)). Colour needs an allow-list (#rgb/#rrggbb) on BOTH generator and page load; mutate each layer separately.
- Origin matters: a file served via Chainglass runs on its origin, so pre-existing innerHTML sinks fed by seat-written structure become real; file:// alone understated it.
- Live probe recipe (no node_modules): generate into mktemp, rewrite fleet-map.data.js with hostile values (bypasses generator checks), inject a probe.js before the data script that dispatches pointer/mouse events on every [data-key] and records #card innerHTML + window.PWN into a body attribute; run `Google Chrome --headless=new --user-data-dir=<tmp> --virtual-time-budget=3000 --dump-dom file://...`. `--log-net-log` shows Chrome's own background traffic (update2, variations, accounts) in every run: diff against a control, don't read it as page requests.
- Generated templates hid external loads (Google Fonts) — grep the template for http(s)://, url(, @import, fetch before claiming "nothing external".
